Article Title: 'Pellet guns can be used in exceptional situations': SC seeks RAF ammunition log from Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:
SC directs Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday observed that police are "empowered to use pellet guns in exceptional situations" while directing the Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) deployed at Jantar Mantar.The court's observation comes at a time when allegations of pellet gun use against NEET protesters during the CJP-led student protest on July 20 have escalated into a political potboiler in Parliament.A Bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed the Delhi government to provide adequate treatment to those protesters who were injured by alleged firing of pellet guns.The bench also observed that when in extreme violent situations police are permitted to use bullets if violence does not get controlled by lathicharge and tear gas, how can they be barred from using pellet guns if a protest, which has turned violent after being hijacked by miscreants for ulterior purposes. The court said all injured persons during protests should be given proper treatment.The top court, however, questioned petitioner and ex-IPS offier Yashovardhan Azad for seeking ban on use of pellet guns against protesters.Meanwhile, a CRPF post-event analysis has said that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun.CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob.Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.Moreover, CRPF director general G P Singh came forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties.Addressing personnel at CRPF investiture ceremony coinciding with its Raising Day Monday, Singh said, "As DG of CRPF, I want to assure each one of you that whether it is an operational battalion or law-and-order unit, whatever decisions you carry out in the bona fide discharge of your duties and which are aligned with interests of the public, the force and the nation, I shall take responsibility for all those decisions and actions. Continue to perform your duties fearlessly. Wherever responsibility or accountability needs to be taken, I will take as the director general".
Article Summary: SC directs Centre to preserve the ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force. Allegations of pellet gun use against NEET protesters have escalated into a political potboiler. CRPF post-event analysis has said that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed.

Article Title: 'Students deserve justice': Rahul Gandhi shares video claiming police brutality during NEET protest
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi seeks SC-monitored probe into police action on students

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Thursday demanded an independent Supreme Court-monitored high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police excesses against students protesting the perpetual paper leaks on July 20."Students deserve justice. An independent SC monitored high powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students," Rahul said in a post on X while sharing a video claiming police brutality during the protest.The remarks came after Rahul had earlier accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of being responsible for the police's alleged excesses against protesters, including the reported firing incident.Rahul demanded the removal of Union home minister Amit Shah and called for a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the alleged use of "lethal force" against student protesters, escalating the Opposition's attack on the government over the police crackdown.Addressing the Lok Sabha, Rahul alleged that Shah either directly authorised the use of pellet guns, shock batons, lathicharge and tear gas against students, making him "culpable of brutalisation" of young protesters, or was unaware of the police action, which, he said, made him "incompetent.""In either case, he has to go," Rahul said, urging Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove the senior minister from the Cabinet.The allegations triggered strong protests from the treasury benches, with Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju demanding that Gandhi either substantiate his claims with evidence or apologise.Rahul Gandhi also blamed RSS for what he described as the problems afflicting the education sector.The government strongly objected to his remarks, with treasury bench members demanding that he either substantiate his allegations or apologise. They said Rahul Gandhi should not be allowed to continue his speech unless he provided evidence or expressed regret for the claims."You cannot level a charge to grab a headline and get away with it without providing proof," Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said.Union minister Jitendra Singh also said that orders for police firing are issued by a magistrate. Defending the Delhi Police, he said the force had exercised "utmost restraint" while handling the protesters' march on July 20, marking the first such defence by a senior government functionary.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi demands an independent Supreme Court-monitored high-powered committee to investigate alleged police excesses. Rahul had earlier accused Union Home Minister Amit Shah of being responsible for the police's alleged excesses against protesters, including the reported firing incident.

Article Title: 'Even Mughals called Shivaji a chuha': Uddhav likens Gen Z to Maratha warrior
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Wednesday likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj , saying that even Mughals had called the Maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat), just as the current generation is being called "cockroaches".Addressing a gathering during a book launch in Mumbai, Thackeray said those who had been dismissed as "cockroaches" belonged to Generation Z, roughly between the ages of 13 and 28 and drew a parallel how Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was only 17 when he captured Torna Fort, while Sant Dnyaneshwar was also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari."Those who were insulted as 'cockroaches' belong to what we now call Generation Z roughly from the ages of thirteen or fourteen to twenty-seven or twenty-eight. Wasn't Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj just about that age when he captured Torna Fort at seventeen? Even Shivaji Maharaj was called a 'Chuha' by Mughal. Wasn't Sant Dnyaneshwar also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari? Both faced tremendous opposition in their own time," Thackeray said.He said Shivaji Maharaj had challenged the Mughal Empire despite his young age, arguing that today's youth should not be belittled for speaking out.This comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted Gen Z terminology to sharpen their political messaging during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.From treasury bench members defending the Centre's reforms to opposition MPs criticising the government's handling of the NEET controversy, lawmakers turned to internet slang more commonly associated with social media than parliamentary debate.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj invoked Gen Z slang while backing the proposed legislation, using the phrase "clock it", a popular internet expression used to acknowledge or recognise something.Speaking in support of the Bill, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution."On the other hand, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra invoked Gen Z terminology while criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach, arguing that young people were able to see through political messaging."If you want to win over the Gen Z, then making videos with different camera angles will not help. The prime minister needs to change the angle of his heart, not the angle of cameras," Priyanka said."Injustice has been done with youths under your government, accept the truth. Prime Minister Narendra Modi must take responsibility," she added.
Article Summary: Uddhav Thackeray likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He said that even Mughals had called the Maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat) This comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted Gen Z terminology.

Article Title: Supreme Court relaxes order mandating Coalgate appeals only before itself, allows Delhi high court to hear them
Article Text:
Apex court on Coalgate case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Diluting its 12year-old order mandating appeals to be filed only in the Supreme Court against trial court orders in coal block allotment scam cases, the SC Wednesday said the prosecution and accused can move the Delhi HC challenging acquittals or convictions recorded by the special judge.Taking up the long pending appeals in coal scam cases, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Why did the Supreme Court invite such a burden on itself ? There may have been certain concerns at some point of time. But can the Supreme Court denude the high court’s constitutionally conferred powers to hear appeals against trial court orders? Powers of the high court to hear appeals against trial court is part of the basic structure. ”Appearing for some of the accused in coal scam cases, senior advocate Kapil Sibal said SC should not be the first forum of appeal against trial court orders. However, SC-appointed special public prosecutor R S Cheema said trials in two-thirds of the cases have been over and that the restraint on approaching the high court against interim orders of the special judge should continue.The bench agreed with Cheema but said that in those cases where the trial court has recorded either conviction or acquittal, the appeal by person or prosecution must challenge it before the Delhi high court.In Sept 2014, Supreme Court had cancelled 204 of the 218 coal block allocations and directed that all appeals against framing of charge, quashing of case and bail petitions must be filed only before the Supreme Court and not Delhi high court.This restriction was imposed to prevent accused from delaying trials.Sibal, who was a minister in the Congress-headed UPA govt when the coal scam and 2G scam cases rocked its electoral support base, told the court that the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) had made an omnibus calculation about alleged loss to exchequer because of the coal block allocations, without quantifying loss attributable to individual coal blocks.“We have challenged the basis on which such calculations were made by the CAG. Moreover, we have also questioned whether mere allotment of coal blocks would amount to corrupt practice without any mining having taken place at all,” Sibal said.The top court asked Cheema and the counsel for accused to help in categorizing the bunch of cases for hearing from Aug 18.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says prosecution and accused can move the Delhi HC challenging acquittals or convictions recorded by the special judge. In Sept 2014, Supreme Court had cancelled 204 of the 218 coal block allocations and directed that all appeals against framing of charge, quashing of case and bail petitions must be filed only before the Supreme Court.

Article Title: Automakers silent on E20 petrol due to government pressure: Kejriwal

NEW DELHI: AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal Wednesday alleged that Centre was pressuring automobile manufacturers to remain silent on the impact of E20 petrol on vehicles manufactured before 2023, a charge rejected by Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra, who challenged him to produce evidence of vehicles damaged due to ethanol-blended fuel.Addressing a news conference, Kejriwal said he had written to 29 companies manufacturing two-wheelers and four-wheelers asking whether E20 petrol could be safely used in vehicles manufactured before 2023, and whether they would compensate consumers if such vehicles suffered damage or lower fuel efficiency.He claimed none of the companies responded in writing, but officials from nine companies spoke to him on the phone. Quoting those officials, Kejriwal alleged that using E20 in vehicles manufactured before 2023 could damage the engine and fuel system and reduce fuel efficiency.He further alleged that Centre had warned automobile companies against making such claims publicly, saying their plants could face action by agencies such as ED, CBI and income tax department.He claimed that companies were being pressured to certify that E20 petrol was safe, but Nitin Gadkari and Arvind Kejriwal were reluctant to do so as consumers could seek compensation or replacement of vehicles if damaged, and that Centre’s decision to impose E20 petrol would turn nearly 30 crore pre-2023 vehicles into scrap.Hitting back, Delhi BJP chief Harsh Malhotra said “I again challenge Arvind Kejriwal...to publicly bring forward 100 vehicles with mechanic certification that the vehicle has been damaged due to ethanol mixed petrol.”

Article Title: Over 1 lakh schools in India functioning with a single teacher
Article Text:
File photo

The single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability

‘Vacancies due to retirement, resignations, enrolment change’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than one lakh schools — government, government-aided and private — are functioning with a single teacher, with Andhra Pradesh alone accounting for over 16,000, government data has revealed, highlighting severe deployment gaps despite the country’s overall pupil-teacher ratio remaining within national norms.The education ministry cited national pupil-teacher ratios of 19 at primary level, 17 at upper primary, 15 at secondary and 23 at higher secondary — all within the limits envisaged under National Education Policy. However, the single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability.According to UDISE+ data for 2025-26, India has 1,00,843 single-teacher schools across all management categories. Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools — more than 16% of the national total — followed by Jharkhand (9,827) and Maharashtra (9,269). Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, UP 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Together, these seven states account for nearly 65% of all schools operating with one teacher.The problem is spread across regions rather than being confined to poorer or geographically difficult states.Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159. Himachal Pradesh has 3,128, Uttarakhand 2,655 and Chhattisgarh 2,461. At the other end, Kerala reported 67 singleteacher schools, Nagaland 35, Sikkim 31, Ladakh 28, Delhi seven and Andaman and Nicobar Islands one.The figures were provided by MoS for education Jayant Chaudhary in response to a RS question on teacher vacancies. While the question sought data specifically for government schools, the annexure on single-teacher institutions covers schools under all managements.The ministry did not provide state-wise sanctioned posts or vacancies, saying recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers were handled by state governments and UT administrations. It attributed vacancies to retirement, resignation, creation of posts, staff rationalisation and changing enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts.Government said states were regularly advised to fill posts through transparent, merit-based recruitment and use technology for forecasting teacher requirements. Financial support was also provided under Samagra Shiksha to maintain prescribed pupil-teacher ratios.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools. Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, UP 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159.

NEW DELHI: As personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF , face questions for having fired pellet guns at anti-NEET paper leak protesters, CRPF director general G P Singh has come forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties.Addressing personnel at CRPF investiture ceremony coinciding with its Raising Day Monday, Singh said, "As DG of CRPF, I want to assure each one of you that whether it is an operational battalion or law-and-order unit, whatever decisions you carry out in the bona fide discharge of your duties and which are aligned with interests of the public, the force and the nation, I shall take responsibility for all those decisions and actions. Continue to perform your duties fearlessly. Wherever responsibility or accountability needs to be taken, I will take as the director general".As TOI reported on Wednesday, a CRPF post-event assessment has found that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and laid down protocols were followed by RAF personnel during the police action against anti-NEET protesters on July 20.In view of this, a source told TOI, no case may be made out against the RAF personnel for causing injuries to 3-5 protesters by firing the metal pellets."Even if a case is registered against the RAF personnel under Section 117 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 218 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita will kick in, mandating grant of prosecution sanction with approval to the CRPF DG. At this point, the DG can justify the use of authorised force by RAF personnel, to deny prosecution sanction," said an officer.CRPF probe into July 20 police action, as per sources, has concluded that the force gradient was followed, with pellet guns being used after lower-grade measures like crowd dispersal warnings, tear gas and lathicharge failed to control the unruly elements in the mob.As required by SOP, Delhi police DCP/ACP had, using his delegated authority as executive magistrate, authorised RAF in a signed format, to use civilian force, including firing pellet guns.
Article Summary: CRPF director general G P Singh has come forward to support all his troops taking decisions and actions in bona fide discharge of their duties. A CRPF post-event assessment has found that all standard operating procedures (SOPs) and laid down protocols were followed.

Article Title: Ground zero of Assam’s flood fury: Village vanishes in an hour; toll rises to 78, over 3L affected
Article Text:
Livelihoods? lost to raging waters

Flood toll rises to 78

, over 3L affected





GUWAHATI: Hiloni Nepali Khuti, a thriving village in Assam's Sivasagar district, along the banks of the Dikhow river, consisting of around 200 Gorkha families, has been wiped out by the devastating floods.Once a hamlet of happy souls, it is now reduced to just a barren stretch of sand and debris.Located barely 500 metres from the Dikhow and 3 km from the Assam-Nagaland border, Hiloni Nepali Khuti's fortunes changed forever on the fateful afternoon of July 19, when the river tore through its settlements and swept away homes and families, after a bout of torrential rain in Nagaland led to a massive increase in its volume.Until that morning, the river was a familiar and friendly sight, but all that changed after it rendered an entire settlement, relying primarily on dairy farming to Nazira and nearby towns, homeless.On that fateful morning, the villagers had gone to collect logs and firewood from the Naga Hills downstream - an annual monsoon ritual. Moments later disaster struck, when the river tore through the village and swept away homes, cattle sheds and nearly 4,000 cattle.Today, with only a handful of livestock, the residents are trying to claw their way back to normalcy, albeit with little hope.All the villagers went to collect the logs and firewood carried by the river from Nagaland hills.We collect those every monsoon. We were very happy. But, we noticed rapid increase in water level and increase in quantity of firewood in the water. Thereafter, the water engulfed the entire village and swept everything without leaving an opportunity for us to save our belongings," Balaram Sharma (38), a resident, said.His family took refuge for two days at an elevated landing in his residence, before they were rescued on the third day. He sent his elderly parents, wife and 3-year-old daughter to Namrup in Dibrugarh. He had 23 cattle, of which 16 were swept away by the floods.Similar to Balaram, Prakash Sharma (35), too, managed to save his family members, but lost 56 of his 60 cattle to the Dikhow's outburst. He saved his four cattle with the help of security forces on July 27, eight days after the floods had hit their village.Assam’s flood death toll rose to 78 on Wednesday after three more bodies — two in Sivasagar and one in Golaghat —were recovered, even as over three lakh people remained affected across seven districts.According to ASDMA, the floods have affected 3,00,031 people in 551 villages under 21 revenue circles. The deluge has also inundated 21,523.08 hectares of cropland.
Article Summary: Hiloni Nepali Khuti, a thriving village in Assam's Sivasagar district, along the banks of the Dikhow river, has been wiped out by the devastating floods. A bout of torrential rain in Nagaland led to a massive increase in the volume of the river. The villagers had gone to collect logs and firewood from the Naga Hills downstream.

Article Title: 'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Article Text:
BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha member Bansuri Swaraj on Tuesday used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi against the paper leak. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill, a term used by the younger generation to recognize a fact.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution"."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure time-bound investigations, speedy trials and tougher penalties for paper leaks and organised exam fraud.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday the formation of a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to overhaul India's examination system and make it more transparent, reliable and technology-driven.Addressing students through a video message, PM Modi said the Centre had already taken steps to curb exam malpractice by jailing those involved, setting up fast-track courts and proposing stricter legal provisions, but stressed that broader systemic reforms were now needed.He said the task force would recommend measures to strengthen the credibility of public examinations, with the government acting on its report at the earliest. The Nilekani-led panel will study the use of technology and suggest reforms to improve transparency, efficiency and trust in the conduct of public examinations.The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the NEET row, as the Centre seeks to restore confidence in the system.
Article Summary: Bansuri Swaraj used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill. The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act.

Article Title: Rs 28.5 crore cash, Rs 21.5 crore gold: Police raid retired bus driver's house in West Bengal
Article Text:
Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.





SURI: Birbhum police on Wednesday raided the house of a retired govt bus driver in Deucha village and seized gold bars and biscuits worth around Rs 21.5 crore, along with two trunkloads of cash. The cash haul had crossed Rs 28.5 crore by late evening, with bundles of notes still being counted.Officers said Minar Mondal, owner of the two-storey house and a relative of influential stone trader Tulu Mondal, and his son were being questioned about the source of the seized wealth and whether they had stashed money and gold at any other location.Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.The entire area was cordoned off for the search, which began in the early hours. Several high-ranking district police officers, including ASP Nilesh Gaikwad and DSP (law and order) Kunal Mukherjee, supervised the raid.Minar’s kin Tulu Mondal, a prominent stone trader in the district, was a stone revenue collector during the tenure of the Trinamool govt. Sources said that after retiring from his govt job, Minar was assigned a key responsibility by Tulu.“Minar was in charge of collecting revenue from stone-filled trucks at one of the seven toll gates in the quarry belt of Deucha. Investigators are trying to find out whether he had siphoned off a chunk of the money meant for the govt coffers,” a source said.Tulu was considered a close associate of Anubrata Mondal, once a Trinamool strongman in the district. He was accused of operating illegal stone quarries and implicated in a cattle smuggling case.ED had raided his home and office in 2022. Within 48 hours of the raid, the district police arrested him in a murder case. He was released on bail and allegedly went into hiding after the assembly poll results were declared on May 4.Tulu had grabbed eyeballs in Dec 2024 by hosting a lavish reception for his daughter’s wedding. Celebrities from Bollywood and the Bengali entertainment industry attended the reception in an extravagant venue modelled on the iconic Taj Lake Palace in Udaipur.CM Suvendu Adhikari thanked police for Wednesday’s operation.He posted on X, “The work of our law enforcement agencies in taking strict action against the sand mafia is commendable. Birbhum Police conducted a major raid at the hideout of illegal operator Tulu Mondal — alias Mohammad Najibuddin — in the Mohammad Bazar police station area.”He wrote, “Let it be unequivocally clear: no person with a chequered past who has amassed wealth through the exploitation of public resources and hobnobbing with the then ruling political party will be spared.”He commended the director general of police, superintendent of Birbhum police and district police personnel for the success of the operation.Kunal Ghosh, spokesperson for the Trinamool faction loyal to Mamata Banerjee, said that while those responsible for such crimes should not be spared, the govt should also investigate netas who allegedly patronised such activities.“I hear that those responsible for such crimes were closely linked to netas who now brand themselves as ‘good Trinamool’. I will urge the govt to delve deeper and identify those who shielded such criminals and benefited from their illegal earnings,” he said.
Article Summary: The cash haul had crossed Rs 28.5 crore by late evening, with bundles of notes still being counted. The entire area was cordoned off for the search, which began in the early hours. Five cash-counting machines and several gold-weighing scales were used to assess the worth of the haul.

NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. The Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.

NEW DELHI: In a major reform, the Centre has introduced one-time physical reporting for NEET-UG counselling, ending repeated visits to allotted medical colleges for candidates seeking a seat upgrade.Aspirants allotted a seat in the first or second round can now complete subsequent reporting and document verification online while retaining their seat for further rounds.Under the new framework, candidates opting for the “Float” option can complete document verification online and receive provisional admission while retaining their allotted seat for subsequent rounds. If allotted a better seat, the earlier one will automatically be released to another candidateThose choosing the “Freeze” option, or retaining a seat after the third round, must report physically to complete admission formalities, including verification of original documents and payment of fees.The reforms were reviewed by Union health minister J P Nadda on Wednesday ahead of the start of NEETUG counselling.“Earlier, every candidate allotted a seat had to physically report to the college even if they wanted to participate in the next round for a better option,” said Dr B Srinivas, deputy director general (medical education), ministry of health and family welfare.“Now, they can complete document verification online, retain the allotted seat and continue in the counselling process.If they get a better seat, the earlier one will be released to another candidate. If not, they will retain their original seat.”The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has also introduced online resignation, allowing eligible candidates to surrender their allotted seat through the counselling portal instead of visiting the institute. Another major change is the complete digitisation of admissions under the NRI category.Candidates requiring additional eligibility documents will now upload them through a dedicated portal instead of sending them by email. “Earlier, these documents sometimes landed in spam folders or were missed, delaying verification. The new software allows direct online verification...” Srinivas said.To improve transparency, the counselling system will use pre-populated candidate data from the National Testing Agency, online document verification, NMC-validated seat matrices and enhanced cybersecurity measures developed with the National Informatics Centre.The Centre has also raised the number of assessment centres for persons with benchmark disabilities (PwBD) from 16 to 61 and introduced an Appellate Disability Assessment Board under revised NMC guidelines.Nadda directed officials to ensure a transparent, meritbased counselling process.
Article Summary: Aspirants allotted a seat in the first or second round can now complete subsequent reporting and document verification online while retaining their seat for further rounds. If allotted a better seat, the earlier one will automatically be released to another candidate. The reforms were reviewed by Union health minister J P Nadda on Wednesday.

NEW DELHI: A DGCA-ordered probe by Boeing into the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the B787 Dreamliner has found “no abnormality”, govt told Parliament on Wednesday.The regulator had ordered this repeat examination after the crew operating an AI Dreamliner from London to Bengaluru in Feb had observed an issue with the switch after landing safely and had reported the same.The switches, which control fuel supply to engines, have been under scrutiny after AI 171 crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad in June 2025 as its engines had run out of fuel. While the incident is still being probed, the locking system of fuel control switches has been probed multiple times since then to ensure safety.Dreamliners operating around the world are still being looked at by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash. The Dreamliner is the most widely used mid-range wide body aircraft globally.“DGCA, as part of continued airworthiness, directed original equipment manufacturer (OEM) level testing of fuel control switch locking mechanism in Seattle. Detailed examination of fuel control switch including structural integrity of fuel control switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed,” minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol said in reply to a Parliament question Wednesday.The minister, however, added that “further inspection of complete thrust control module at OEM facility is underway”.This module translates pilot inputs or autothrottle commands into precise electronic signals to control engine power.On Feb 2, 2026, the AI Dreamliner on which the crew had reported an issue with the fuel control switch after landing in Bengaluru had been grounded for checks. At that time, AI had said in a statement: “We are aware that one of our pilots has reported a possible defect on the fuel control switch of a Boeing 787 aircraft...We have grounded the said aircraft and are involving the OEM to get the pilot’s concerns checked on a priority basis. The matter has been communicated to the aviation regulator, DGCA. Air India had checked the fuel control switches on all Boeing 787 aircraft in its fleet after a directive from the DGCA, and had found no issues.”On the AI 171 crash, Mohol said Wednesday: “There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process. The final report will be made public and published on AAIB’s website after completion.”

Article Title: Here's why many MBBS graduates can't take foreign licensing exams
Article Text:
The directory lists medical schools recognisedby the local govt or the ministry concerned, globally

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Thousands of students who have completed MBBS are unable to appear for any foreign licensing examination as the colleges they have graduated from have not initiated the process for an "ECFMG sponsor note" in the World Directory of Medical Schools. This is a formal note on a medical college's listing in the world directory indicating that it meets standards set by Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG).The directory aims to list all medical schools which have been recognised by the local govt or ministry concerned, globally. However, colleges listed here might not have sponsor notes that make their students eligible for ECFMG certification, a credential evaluation agency. Colleges can apply electronically for credential verification only after their first batch of graduates, or roughly five years after the first batch is admitted.Usually, colleges start the process when their first batch starts the 12-month compulsory rotating medical internship. However, many students have discovered after MBBS graduation that their colleges have not got ECFMG sponsor notes. Most students who join colleges don't check whether their college has ECFMG sponsor notes till after graduation when they want to sit for USMLE (United States Medical Licensing Examination), UK's PLAB (Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board) or other licensing exams.Many graduates of Kalpana Chawla Medical College in Karnal, Haryana, discovered that their college did not have ECFMG sponsor notes though it admitted its first batch in 2017. Some at AIIMS have not got ECFMG sponsor notes.In response to an RTI query , National Medical Commission (NMC) stated that "as and when any information or documents to update ECFMG sponsor note in respect of Indian medical colleges is asked by ECFMG, the same is provided to ECFMG immediately after due process and approval of competent authority".NMC's response on June 30 stated the submission of information to ECFMG to update sponsor notes on the world directory list was under process in NMC for several colleges.There was no response from NMC and Union health ministry to TOI's queries on whether it was mandated that all Indian medical colleges must apply to ECFMG sponsor notes on time, and on students' complaints on the issue.
Article Summary: Thousands of students unable to appear for foreign licensing exams as colleges have not initiated process for "ECFMG sponsor note" This is a formal note on a medical college's listing in the world directory indicating that it meets standards set by Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates. Colleges can apply electronically for credential verification only after their first batch of graduates.

NEW DELHI: As India moves towards introducing a dengue vaccine by next year, the country's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and UTs, a development researchers say could influence vaccine strategy as infections with multiple strains are associated with more severe disease.The pan-India molecular surveillance study, led by ICMR-National Institute of Virology, Pune, analysed 6,889 lab-confirmed dengue samples collected through 45 virus research and diagnostic laboratories (VRDLs) across 25 states and UTs between 2023 and 2025. It found that dengue serotypes - at least two - were co-circulating in each state and UT included in the surveillance, indicating increasing hyperendemicity of the disease in India.According to the study, all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4) were detected simultaneously in Andhra, Gujarat, Haryana, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. Fifteen other states and UTs had three serotypes in circulation, while two reported circulation of two serotypes.Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain, accounting for 51% of infections, followed by DENV-3 (13%), DENV-1 (7%) and DENV-4 (1%).About 7% of patients were infected with two or more dengue serotypes simultaneously.The study found patients with concurrent infections were more likely to develop thrombocytopenia, haemorrhagic manifestations and arthralgia than those infected with a single serotype, suggesting that circulation of multiple strains could increase the burden of severe dengue.The researchers said continuous molecular surveillance is essential to monitor changing dengue virus circulation, improve outbreak prediction and guide vaccine introduction strategies. They noted that several dengue vaccine candidates are in advanced stages of development and that vaccine efficacy varies against different serotypes, making surveillance critical for immunisation policy.The study also highlighted regional differences in virus circulation. While DENV-2 predominated across India, DENV-1 accounted for a relatively larger share of infections in Tamil Nadu (29%), Haryana (38%) and Rajasthan (25%). DENV-3 was more frequently detected in Gujarat (30%), TN(29%), UP (29%) and WB (20%).
Article Summary: India's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and UTs. Article Title: Supreme Court bars government from post facto green clearance to projects

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday saved central and state projects worth Rs 20,000 crore from demolition for want of prior environmental clearance but permanently prohibited govt from granting post facto EC and quashed Centre’s 2021 Office Memorandum for keeping a window indefinitely open for projects to seek such green nods.Rescinding a part of its earlier decision that had quashed Centre’s 2017 notification, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi said the 2017 notification was valid as it had a limited period window for clearance to projects of significant public interest.However, the bench concurred with the earlier decision to quash the 2021 OM as finding it to be an open-ended administrative order was tantamount to a perpetual amnesty regime for grant of EC to projects undertaken without prior green nod. It said the OM was without having any rational nexus with public interest, and hence is in breach of Environment Protection Act, 1986.Supreme Court said its judgment will operate prospectively, and the ECs granted to various projects under the 2017 notification and the 2021 OM would remain valid. “The prior EC regime under the 2006 notification is mandatory and unless amended by an appropriate notification, would not accommodate grant of post facto EC or retention of projects where constructions have commenced or processes begun without a valid EC,” it said.Supreme Court directed scrupulous adherence to the 2006 notification mandating prior EC clearance for projects. The bench said, “Govt is restrained from issuing administrative orders in future for grant of EC in respect of projects which have commenced in contravention of the prior EC regime under the 2006 notification.”Pending applications (for grant of post facto EC) shall be dealt with in accordance with the law, it said, adding that “no fresh application for grant of EC under the aforesaid instruments (2014 notification or 2021 OM) shall be entertained.”Writing the judgment, Justice Bagchi said the court aimed to strike a balance between an “existential right of all living beings both present and future to a pollution-free environment and an aspirational right to development of a sixth of the world’s population”.The bench, however, noted that Centre has powers under Jan Vishwas Act to decriminalise violations of EP Act by notifying amnesty schemes with regard to such classes or categories of non-compliant projects whose sustainability is necessary to subserve larger public interest.In Nov last year, a bench of then CJI B R Gavai and Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and K Vinod Chandran by two to one majority decided to review the court’s May 2025 decision by Justices A S Oka and Bhuyan which had quashed all post facto green clearance which left public projects worth Rs 20,000 crore vulnerable to demolition.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes Centre’s 2021 Office Memorandum for keeping a window indefinitely open for projects to seek green nods. It said the OM was without having any rational nexus with public interest, and hence is in breach of Environment Protection Act, 1986.

Article Title: Supreme Court curbs powers of SC panel, says it can’t pass adjudicatory orders

NEW DELHI: Limiting the power of National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), Supreme Court has held that it is a recommendatory and advisory body and does not have the authority to pass an adjudicatory order.Abench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said the commission can send its recommendations to a state or Centre in discharge of its functions. However, an order passed by NCSC is not binding in servicerelated matters, it clarified.“The powers entrusted to NCSC are limited in nature. Clearly, NCSC and its other compatriots under articles 338A and 338B are constitutional bodies with a socially beneficent purpose but quite apparently, the legislature has prescribed a role that is recommendatory and advisory, but certainly not adjudicatory. They are not meant to be bodies taking over adjudicatory functions,” the bench said.The court’s order could be applicable to other statutory and constitutional bodies set up for the benefit of different groups of people like women, the minorities and backward classes.Explaining the clause which says that the commission is empowered to “inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes”, the bench said, “it is therefore clear that while it has powers to requisition documents and receive evidence, it does not have the power to make an order in furtherance of that evidence.In other words, NCSC can record a factual finding and then ask the govt concerned, either the Centre or the State, to act thereupon.”It rejected NCSC’s plea that the word “safeguards” mentioned in the provision pertains to enforcement. “Such a submission is difficult to accept in view of the explicit language of the Article. It certainly does not confer adjudicatory power; at best recommendatory in nature,” the court said.Thus, the commission cannot take up the role of a court or an adjudicatory tribunal and determine the rights of parties, court added.
Article Summary: National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) is a recommendatory and advisory body and does not have the authority to pass an adjudicatory order. The court’s order could be applicable to other statutory and constitutional bodies set up for the benefit of different groups of people.

NEW DELHI: Rejecting a plea seeking a ban on release of an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath, Supreme Court on Wednesday said artists must enjoy the liberty of creative expression, with courts not getting in the way of art and creativity.As Jagannath temple committee strongly opposed the release of the animation film, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that if depiction of gods and goddesses is prevented, then movies on the Ramayana and Mahabharata would not be made and screened at all. NEW DELHI: In a move aimed at reducing the compliance burden and improving ease of doing business for vehicle manufacturers, the road transport ministry has proposed changes to the conformity of production (CoP) regime for emission compliance for new and existing vehicle models.Under the draft proposal, the CoP test for emission compliance of new models of passenger cars and two-wheelers will be conducted annually for the first three years after type approval and thereafter once every three years. For larger passenger vehicles, goods vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles, the CoP test will continue to be conducted annually.For existing models, the testing frequency will be reduced to once every three years for two-wheelers, passenger cars, larger passenger vehicles, goods vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles.At present, the CoP test for all passenger car models is conducted annually, while for two-wheelers—which are produced in much larger volumes—the testing frequency ranges from once every three months to once a year, depending on production volume.CoP is a regulatory verification process that ensures mass-produced vehicles continue to conform to their original type-approval specifications.“The proposed policy delinks the CoP testing frequency from the volume of vehicles produced or imported. Manufacturers and importers will need to strengthen their quality control systems and ensure continued compliance with the norms, as any defect or deviation detected after three years could expose them to the risk of recalling a large number of vehicles, particularly two-wheelers,” an official said.Under the CoP regime, testing agencies randomly pick vehicles from assembly lines, dealerships or the open market for emission compliance tests, with the entire cost of testing being borne by vehicle manufacturers.
Article Summary: The road transport ministry has proposed changes to the conformity of production (CoP) regime. CoP is a regulatory verification process that ensures mass- produced vehicles continue to conform to their original type-approval specifications. At present, the CoP test for all passenger car models is conducted annually.

Article Title: MP farmers breach barricades, reach within 1 km of CM Mohan Yadav's residence over moong MSP
Article Text:
MP farmers breach barricades, march towards CM Mohan Yadav's residence over moong MSP. (PTI images)

NEW DELHI: Hundreds of farmers protesting over the procurement of summer moong at the minimum support price (MSP) breached multiple police barricades and marched to Roshanpura Square in Bhopal on Wednesday, reaching within a kilometre of Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav's official residence.Before reaching Roshanpura, the protesters demonstrated outside Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan's residence as the state government initiated talks with farmer representatives.Led by the Samyukta Kisan Morcha and 18 other farmer organisations, the protesters crossed several layers of barricades on Narmadapuram Road, resulting in tense stand-offs with police. Authorities deployed heavy security at Roshanpura Square, where the farmers camped while negotiations continued at the state secretariat.Although repeated scuffles broke out between protesters and police and the windows of a few buses were damaged, police did not resort to force.The farmers are demanding procurement of the entire summer moong crop at MSP, the scrapping of the e-token system for fertiliser distribution and timely availability of fertilisers ahead of the next sowing season.In an attempt to resolve the standoff, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced the formation of a four-member committee to hold discussions with farmer representatives."The government has always stood with farmers and is ready to consider positive suggestions. At the same time, both sides should ensure that the public doesn’t face inconvenience. We will resolve the issue through talks," Yadav said.He expressed hope that the Bharatiya Kisan Sangathan and other organisations would resolve the issue through dialogue, adding that the government's commitment to public welfare also included farmers' welfare.Despite the government's outreach, some protesters intensified the agitation by staging a semi-nude demonstration on Narmadapuram Road. Protesters also performed a 'Sadbuddhi Yagya' and cooked baati-chokha on the roadside, while residents, including members of Generation Z, extended support to the agitation.The protest continued after the first round of talks between State Agriculture Minister Aidal Singh Kansana and farmer leaders ended without a breakthrough on Tuesday night. Farmers remained on the roads overnight, disrupting traffic and prompting police to divert commuters. Schools in nearby areas remained closed on Wednesday morning.Meanwhile, Kansana wrote to Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan seeking an increase in the procurement limit for summer moong.Responding after protesters gathered outside his residence, Chouhan said the Centre had already approved procurement of up to 4,54,580 tonnes of summer moong for Madhya Pradesh under the Price Support Scheme for the 2025-26 season.He said the allocation accounted for 87 per cent of the total 5,23,243 tonnes approved nationwide under the PM-AASHA scheme, the highest allocation for any state.Chouhan also clarified that the Centre does not prescribe procurement targets for states. Under PM-AASHA guidelines, procurement is allowed up to 25 per cent of estimated production, with any procurement beyond that limit to be undertaken by the state government.According to data available with the Centre until July 29, Madhya Pradesh had procured around 60,000 tonnes of summer moong so far, Chouhan said, urging the state government to speed up procurement in the interest of farmers.
Article Summary: MP farmers breach barricades, march towards CM Mohan Yadav's residence over moong MSP. Authorities deployed heavy security at Roshanpura Square, where the farmers camped while negotiations continued at the state secretariat. The farmers are demanding procurement of the entire summer moong crop at MSP, the scrapping of the e-token system for fertiliser distribution and timely availability of fertilisers.

Article Title: Use of maize & rice for ethanol production sees huge jump

NEW DELHI: While the use of rice, maize and damaged food grain for ethanol manufacturing has increased manifold in the past six years, maize has surpassed rice sold by Food Corporation of India (FCI) to distilleries under govt’s ethanol blended petrol (EBP) programme.Food ministry’s data submitted to Lok Sabha on Wednesday show that till June end of the current 2025-26 ethanol supply year (Oct to Sept), a little over 54 lakh tonne of FCI’s surplus rice and damaged foodgrain (including broken rice) had been used by distilleries under EBP programme, while the figure for maize was around 68 lakh tonne. Two months of the current ethanol supply year (ESY) are still left.Data show that there was no use of maize for ethanol manufacturing during ESY of 2020-21 and 2021-22. After a modest start in ESY 2022-23 with 8.3 lakh tonne of maize being used for manufacturing the bio-fuel, the figure jumped to 75.4 lakh tonne the next year and 131 lakh tonne in ESY 2024-25, which was an all-time high. In comparison, a little over 50 lakh tonne of FCI’s surplus rice and broken rice was used for ethanol production in 2024-25.The ministry said, “Diversification of feedstock base for ethanol production to sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses, C-heavy molasses, maize, damaged food grains, surplus FCI rice has reduced dependence on any single feedstock or crop and has supported agricultural diversification.”It added that inclusion of maize as a feedstock for ethanol production has helped provide farmers with assured markets and ensured better prices.FCI sells surplus rice for ethanol production after meeting the requirements under National Food Security Act and other welfare schemes and maintaining a buffer stock, the ministry stated. FCI had stopped supply of rice for ethanol production during ESY 2022-23.As per sugar industry, only 2,890 million litres of ethanol, just 28% of the total requirement, are to be procured from sugar-based feedstocks for ESY 2025–26, compared to 72% or 7,610 million litres from grain-based sources, of which 4,780 million litres are from maize (45%), and 2,830 million litres from rice (22%).On Tuesday, govt informed Rajya Sabha that FCI had sold rice to ethanol distilleries at Rs 2,250-2,320 per quintal during June 2025–June 2026, about 40% below its acquisition cost of Rs 3,720-3,889 a quintal. FCI’s average acquisition cost includes MSP and storage and carrying costs.
Article Summary: maize has surpassed rice sold by Food Corporation of India (FCI) to distilleries under govt’s ethanol blended petrol (EBP) programme. till June end of the current 2025-26 ethanol supply year (Oct to Sept), a little over 54 lakh tonne of FCI's surplus rice and damaged foodgrain (including broken rice) had been used.
